newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER'S INCE GETS FOUR-MATCH BAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER'S INCE GETS FOUR-MATCH BAN.

text.p: Internazionale and England midfielder Paul Ince was given a four-match ban on Monday for protesting with foul language and abusive gestures after he was sent off in an Italian league match.
Ince, picking up his third red card of the season, was sent off during Inter's 1-1 draw with bottom club Reggiana on December 22 after being booked by referee Stefano Farina.
The serie A sporting judge said in a report, details of which were released by the Italian soccer league, that Ince had been given the ban because of his behaviour.
The report said Ince had applauded the referee mockingly after being booked, a gesture that brought him a red card and which prompted "vulgar and offensive language".
It added that Ince, encouraged to leave the pitch by his team mates, then repeatedly tapped his forehead with his index finger in front of another match official.
The player also "shouted further abuse while making an unmistakeable gesture with his hand" from the tunnel.

Inter striker Marco Branca, who was sent off in the 30th minute of the match, was also suspended for one day -- leaving Inter without two key players for their first league match of the New Year at home to Roma, Branca's former club.
The lengthy suspension of Ince was also sure to heighten speculation about the player's future in Italy.

Italian newspapers, picking up English media reports, on Monday ran stories suggesting that Ince, who has been the target of some racist abuse in Italy, was thinking of returning to English soccer at the end of the Italian season.
Ince's contract at Inter runs to 1999 and he has become a firm favourite of the fans at the San Siro stadium.
